name: llama.cpp server (observability surface: 14 hand-built Prometheus metrics, off by default, no OTel)
notable_features: The whole /metrics body is built by hand in server_task_result_metrics::to_metrics() with string concatenation - there is no Prometheus client library and no multiprocess mode, so there is no label cardinality and no pid label

4 gauges: `llamacpp:prompt_tokens_seconds` (average prompt throughput tok/s), `llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds` (average generation throughput tok/s), `llamacpp:requests_processing`, `llamacpp:requests_deferred`, plus `llamacpp:n_busy_slots_per_decode`
Slot-level state is exposed as JSON on `GET /slots` (enabled by default, unlike /metrics) with per-slot id, n_ctx, is_processing, sampling params, next_token and a timings object
In router mode, /metrics requires ?model={model_id} and returns HTTP 400 'model name is missing from the request' without it - so a multi-model deployment needs one scrape target per model
hardware_caveats: Prometheus is OFF by default: `--metrics` 'enable prometheus compatible metrics endpoint (default: disabled)' (env LLAMA_ARG_ENDPOINT_METRICS). A reader arriving at a stock llama.cpp server finds no metrics endpoint at all

NO TTFT, NO TPOT, NO ITL, NO queue time, NO KV cache utilization, NO preemption. The metric set is throughput and slot occupancy only. The per-request timings object on the chat/completions response (prompt_ms, prompt_per_second, predicted_ms, predicted_per_token_ms, predicted_per_second, cache_n) is response data, not an exported series, so time-to-first-token has to be measured by the client
`llamacpp:requests_deferred` counts tasks deferred rather than waiting, and there is no explicit waiting-queue gauge; in-flight work is `llamacpp:requests_processing` only
In router mode every /metrics request must name a model, and the README notes the router uses the model query parameter (URL-encoded) for GET endpoints including /metrics
`llamacpp:prompt_tokens_seconds` and `llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds` are lifetime averages from a token bucket, not instantaneous rate - a rolling-average gauge that will lag a traffic change
best_for: A local or edge deployment where you want to know it is doing work at all: tokens processed, decode calls made, slots busy
Single-process monitoring without a Prometheus dependency - the output is plain text with HELP and TYPE lines that anything can scrape

Confirming that speculative decoding is helping: draft/accepted/step counters, plus a per-position counter `llamacpp:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos_total{position="N"}` that is absent when spec-decode is off
avoid_for: Any latency SLO - there is no latency metric of any kind on /metrics
Multi-tenant capacity planning - no KV cache occupancy, so you cannot tell how close to the context limit you are
Distributed tracing: an in-repo code search for opentelemetry in ggml-org/llama.cpp returns 0 hits. There is no tracing support at all
notes: Transcribed from server_task_result_metrics::to_metrics() in tools/server/server-task.cpp on master and cross-checked against the 'Available metrics' table in tools/server/README.md; the two agree except that the README table omits `llamacpp:prompt_tokens_cached_total` while the code emits it. Two related counters exist: `llamacpp:prompt_tokens_cached_total` ('Number of prompt tokens reused from the cache') and `llamacpp:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos_total{position="N"}`. Note the naming oddity that `llamacpp:n_tokens_max` is emitted as a Counter although it is documented as a high-watermark of observed context size - a monotonic max is legitimately counter-shaped, but the name reads like a gauge. `llamacpp:n_busy_slots_per_decode` is 'Average number of busy slots per llama_decode() call', computed as n_busy_slots / max(n_decode, 1), which is a batching-efficiency signal rather than a latency signal.
